start.title: Patient Presentation
start.narrative: Susan, a 42-year-old female, presents to your clinic with painful and frequent urination.

gather_history.title: Comprehensive History
gather_history.narrative: Select all the historical components you would like to elicit.

onset.label: Onset (O)
onset.finding: Symptoms started abruptly two days ago.

characteristics.label: Characteristics (C)
characteristics.finding: 'Burning' sensation when voiding. Constant urge to pee, cloudy urine.

associated_sx.label: Associated Symptoms
associated_sx.finding: Denies fever, chills, flank pain, or vaginal discharge.

sexual_hx.label: Sexual History
sexual_hx.finding: Sexually active. One new male partner within the last week.

pelvic.label: Pelvic
pelvic.finding: Normal genitalia. No abnormal discharge or cervical motion tenderness.

results_pending.title: Results Pending
results_pending.narrative: Orders have been resulted. Review the 'Lab Results' tab.

select_ddx.title: Differential Diagnosis
select_ddx.prompt: Select the most likely leading diagnosis.

patho_q1.title: Knowledge Check 1: Pathophysiology
patho_q1.narrative: You diagnosed Acute Simple Cystitis. Her cloudy urine and positive nitrites strongly support a bacterial etiology.

decision.prompt: What is the most common pathophysiologic mechanism for this condition?

choices.text: An ascending infection from periurethral/fecal flora.

patho_q2.title: Knowledge Check 2: Symptomatology
patho_q2.narrative: Understanding that pathogens ascend the urethra is key to proper hygiene counseling.

decision.prompt: Susan's urgency and frequency are primarily caused by:

choices.text: Inflammation of the urothelium irritating stretch receptors.
Increased urine production to flush the infection.

patho_q3.title: Knowledge Check 3: Complications
patho_q3.narrative: Because the stretch receptors are irritated, she constantly feels full despite low volumes.

decision.prompt: If untreated, this ascending infection most commonly leads to:
Which urinalysis finding is highly specific for Enterobacteriaceae (like E. coli) over other pathogens?

patho_q5.title: Knowledge Check 5: Treatment
patho_q5.narrative: Nitrite positivity confirms the presence of nitrate-reducing bacteria like E. coli.

decision.prompt: When selecting first-line empiric therapy (e.g., Nitrofurantoin), what is its primary mechanism of action?

choices.text: Damages bacterial DNA and ribosomal proteins.

rationales.Diagnosis: Acute Simple Cystitis: Localized lower tract symptoms with normal vitals and no CVA tenderness.
rationales.Patho_1: Ascending Infection: Most UTIs are caused by fecal flora ascending the short female urethra.
rationales.Patho_2: Symptomatology: Mucosal inflammation lowers the firing threshold of detrusor stretch receptors.
rationales.Patho_3: Complications: Unchecked ascending infections travel up the ureters to cause pyelonephritis.
rationales.Patho_4: Nitrites: E. coli converts urinary nitrates to nitrites. Leukocyte esterase just indicates WBC presence (inflammation).
rationales.Patho_5: Nitrofurantoin: It is reduced by bacterial flavoproteins to reactive intermediates that damage DNA/RNA.

start.title: ED Presentation
start.narrative: Liam, 9, presents with facial puffiness and bloody urine.

urine_changes.label: Urine changes?
urine_changes.finding: Bloody, cola-colored for 24 hours. Oliguria noted.

select_ddx.title: Differential Diagnosis
select_ddx.prompt: Select diagnosis based on elevated ASO, low C3, and edema.

decision.prompt: What primarily drives his periorbital and scrotal edema?

choices.text: Sodium/water retention due to decreased GFR.

patho_q2.title: Knowledge Check 2: Immunology
patho_q2.narrative: Unlike Nephrotic Syndrome, his edema is driven by poor filtration and retention.

decision.prompt: What is the pathophysiological basis for his low C3 complement?

choices.text: Consumption by immune complexes depositing in the glomeruli.

patho_q3.title: Knowledge Check 3: Urinalysis
patho_q3.narrative: The immune complex deposition confirms this as a Type III hypersensitivity reaction.

decision.prompt: What is the specific clinical significance of finding RBC Casts?

choices.text: Proves hematuria is of glomerular origin.

patho_q4.title: Knowledge Check 4: Hemodynamics
patho_q4.narrative: RBC casts form when cells squeeze through the damaged glomerular basement membrane.

decision.prompt: What is the primary cause of his acute hypertension?

patho_q5.title: Knowledge Check 5: Prognosis
patho_q5.narrative: Volume expansion from oliguria drives the blood pressure spike.

decision.prompt: What key pathological feature distinguishes chronic progression from acute resolution?

rationales.Patho_1: Edema: Drops in GFR cause primary sodium retention, increasing hydrostatic pressure.
rationales.Patho_2: Low C3: Consumed by the alternative pathway activated by immune complexes.
rationales.Patho_3: RBC Casts: Hallmarks of glomerular damage; RBCs get trapped in Tamm-Horsfall mucoprotein.
rationales.Patho_4: Hypertension: Driven by fluid overload (hypervolemia) secondary to oliguria.
rationales.Patho_5: Chronicity: Most kids recover fully; chronic disease is marked by permanent scarring.
